d: Rich Text Markup are simple markup tags to style sections of a string.
h:
UI rich text utilizes simple markup tags to style sections of a string in bold, italics, underline, fill color, stroke variations, and more. You can apply styling tags to TextLabel, TextButton, and TextBox objects.

Enable rich text

You must enable rich text on a per-object basis through its RichText property in the Properties window, or by setting the property to true in a LocalScript.

local title = Instance.new("TextLabel")
title.RichText = true

title.Text = "Use a <b>bold title</b>"

When editing an object's Text property in Studio, toggling the RichText checkbox in the Properties window displays the text string as a final render. This is useful for identifying and correcting mistakes in any supported tags.

Localizing a game to support other languages removes rich text formatting tags. To ensure formatting appears in other languages, re-apply the tags manually to your localized strings.

Supported tags

Rich text tags are similar to XML/HTML tags and you must include both an opening and closing tag around the formatted text.

<b>Formatted text</b>

You can also nest tags inside each other as long as you close them in the reverse order of how you opened them.

<b><i><u>Formatted text</u></i></b>

Font color

<font color=""> </font>

`I want the orange candy.`
`I want the orange candy.`

`This is Michroma face.`

Font face/family names are listed on the Font enum reference page.

Font family

<font family=""> </font>

`This is Michroma face.`

Font face/family names are listed on the Font enum reference page.

Font weight

<font weight=""> </font>

`This is normal. This is heavy.`
`This is normal. This is heavy.`

Font weight can be a case-insensitive string name including Thin, ExtraLight, Light, Regular, Medium, SemiBold, Bold, ExtraBold, or Heavy; it can also be a number in factors of 100 between 100 and 900.

Font transparency

<font transparency=""> </font>

`Text at 50% transparency.`

Stroke

<stroke> </stroke>

Parameter Equivalent Property Example Values
`color` UIStroke.Color `"rgb(255,125,0)"`, `"#FF7800"`
`thickness` or `th` UIStroke.Thickness `"1"`, `"4"`, `"0.5"`
`transparency` or `tr` UIStroke.Transparency `"0"`, `"0.5"`, `"1"`
`joins` UIStroke.LineJoinMode `"round"`, `"bevel"`, `"miter"`
`sizing` UIStroke.StrokeSizingMode `"fixed"`, `"scaled"`
`You won 25 gems.`

See UI appearance modifiers for details on <stroke> tag parameters such as thickness and joins.

`Uppercase makes words read loudly!`

Comment

``

`After this is a comment... and now more text...`

Escape forms

If you want to render certain characters like < or > and exempt them from consideration as part of rich text tags, you can write them in their escape form.

Character Escape Example Result
`<` `<` `10 < 100` 10 < 100
`>` `>` `100 > 10` 100 > 10
`"` `"` `Meet "Diva Dragonslayer"` Meet "Diva Dragonslayer"
`'` `'` `Diva's pet is a falcon!` Diva's pet is a falcon!
`&` `&` `Render another escape form < by escaping an ampersand` Render another escape form **<** by escaping an ampersand

kid.simple: Rich text lets you style just part of a sentence on a label, button, or text box. You wrap words in little tags, like `bold` or `orange`, and Roblox draws them styled. You can make words bold, italic, underlined, colored, bigger, outlined, highlighted, and more. It is perfect for things like "You won 25 gems" where the gem count pops out.
kid.analogy: It is like using a highlighter and colored pens on a school worksheet: same page, but certain words stand out because you marked them.
keyPoints: Rich text works on `TextLabel`, `TextButton`, and `TextBox`, but you must turn on the `RichText` property for each object.
Every tag needs an opening and a closing tag, like `` and ``.
You can nest tags, but close them in reverse order: `hi`.

Other tags include `` (outline), ``, ``, ``, ``, `
` (new line), `` (uppercase), `` (small caps), `` (highlight), and `` (hidden comment).
To show the characters `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`, or `&` as plain text, use escape forms like `<` and `&`.
Localizing (translating) your game removes rich text tags, so you need to add the tags back to translated text yourself.

terms.markup tag: A label in angle brackets that tells Roblox how to style text, like `` to start bold and `` to end it.
terms.nest: Put one tag inside another. `Win` is bold and underlined.
terms.stroke: An outline around text. `thickness="2"` makes a 2-pixel outline.
terms.font face: The style of letters, like Michroma or Oswald.
terms.font weight: How thick the letters are, from `100` (thin) to `900` (heavy), or names like `Bold` and `Heavy`.
terms.transparency: How see-through something is. `0` is solid, `0.5` is half see-through, `1` is invisible.
terms.hex color: A color written as `#` plus six characters, like `#FF7800` for orange. You can also use `rgb(255,125,0)`.
terms.escape form: A special code that shows a symbol instead of treating it as part of a tag. `<` shows `<`.
terms.localization: Translating your game into other languages.

example.title: A reward message with a highlighted gem count
example.place: LocalScript inside a ScreenGui in StarterGui
example.code: local screenGui = script.Parent local label = Instance.new("TextLabel") label.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(400, 60) label.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(20, 20) label.TextSize = 28 label.RichText = true -- must be on for tags to work -- Bold the word, color the number gold, and outline it label.Text = "Nice! You won 25 gems" label.Parent = screenGui
explain: We create a `TextLabel` and give it a size, position, and text size.
`RichText = true` tells Roblox to read the tags instead of showing them as letters.
`<font color="#FFCC00">` makes "25 gems" gold, and `<stroke>` adds a 2-pixel black outline around it.
Tags close in reverse order: `</stroke>` comes before `</font>`.

watchOut: Forgetting to turn on `RichText`. Without it, players see the raw tags like `<b>` on screen.
Closing tags in the wrong order, like `text`. Always close the newest tag first.
Missing a closing tag. Every `` needs a ``.
Typing `<` or `&` as normal text in rich text. Use `<` or `&` instead.
Translated text loses its tags. Re-add the tags to your translated strings.
